text.p: Hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti on Tuesday said he was totally opposed to a corrective mini-budget, saying it would be a "serious error".
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition depends on Communist Refoundation for its majority in the chamber of deputies (lower house).
Bertinotti issued a statment after Prodi said a mini-budget this year was "very probable" but not definite.

Bertinotti said it would be a "serious error" to propose a cost-cutting mini-budget after Italians have already been asked to pay a one-off tax to help the government meet criteria for entry into European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The hard-left leader said a mini-budget would generate anti-Europe sentiment in Italy and also once again hit pensioners and salaried workers.
"To hit pensions would only lead to a government crisis," he said.
The government is to decide on the mini-budget in the next few weeks after final 1996 figures are available. --Rome newsroom +396-678-2501
